source.title: For self-supervised learning, Rationality implies generalization, provably
source.authors: Yamini Bansal; Gal Kaplun; B. Barak

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; tables are flattened but their row and column assignments are recoverable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures generalization and random-label fitting for self-supervised-plus-simple classifiers, but it does not test the specific versions’ conditions. Its discussion of Zhang et al.’s supervised random-label result is cited prior work.
record.gate_note: The paper reports generalization-gap tables for many self-supervised classifiers and a random-label experiment. The Inception random-label results are attributed to Zhang et al. and are not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study measures generalization and random-label fitting in frozen self-supervised representations followed by simple classifiers. These differ from V1's end-to-end supervised recipes, and do not satisfy its random-label interpolation condition. The supervised Inception comparison is cited from Zhang et al., not independently measured. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the tested self-supervised-plus-simple classifiers often have small generalization gaps. The authors decompose the gap into robustness, rationality and memorization components, bound memorization using the simple classifier's complexity independently of representation complexity, and obtain non-vacuous generalization bounds when robustness and rationality gaps are small. They acknowledge loose numerical bounds, especially on ImageNet.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates self-supervised representation learning followed by a simple classifier, rather than the end-to-end supervised recipes in the claim versions. It does not directly test any listed version.
record.method_sensitivity: Data augmentation changes the measured gaps: the authors report lower robustness and memorization gaps and higher rationality gap as augmentations increase in their AMDIM CIFAR-10 experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, SimCLR, AMDIM and MoCoV2 with simple linear classifiers achieve random-label train/test accuracies of 22%/10%, 18%/10% and 15%/10%, respectively. Their corresponding clean-label test accuracies are 92%, 87.4% and 67.6%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These frozen self-supervised representations support natural-label classification well above chance while their tested simple classifiers fit only a small fraction of fully randomized labels.

record.problems: The detailed generalization-gap results are presented in tables and figures, and the paper says it did not optimize reimplementations for state-of-the-art performance. The random-label SSS results are averaged over 5 runs; uncertainty intervals are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Tables E.1 and E.2 report per-model generalization gaps and component gaps for many SSS methods. They are not rows here because the study does not test any listed version, and the catalog’s version mapping does not cover these self-supervised-plus-simple comparisons. The Inception random-label result in Table B.1 is explicitly attributed to Zhang et al. (2017), so it is excluded.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same end-to-end supervised recipe; the paper's own SSS methods fit only 15–22% of random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, including interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The random-label experiment is not excluded merely because labels were deliberately randomized: that manipulation is relevant to memorization capacity. Its exclusion from V1 rests on the different training recipe and lack of random-label interpolation. None-linked row states are cannot_determine with respect to the listed versions; the corrected accuracies themselves are readable.

versions.untested_parts: The study’s own random-label experiment uses SSS methods that do not fit random labels nearly perfectly; it does not test the coexistence claim on networks that do.
No width sweep around the interpolation threshold.
No controlled comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures.
Optimizer generalization differences are not tested.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or alternative generalization-measure comparison.

rows.uncertainty: averaged over 5 runs (SSS results); uncertainty not stated for this entry
rows.note: Random-label train accuracy is far below perfect; test accuracy is at chance.
